Krupali N Bhatt learned advocate has entered her appearance on behalf of respondent no.3-Insurance Company.

However, no appearance has been entered on their behalf.

Noticing the limited issue involved and the interest of the respondent being effectively represented by the respondent-Insurance Company, the present appeal is taken for final hearing in their absence.

2. The present appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 at the instance of the original claimants being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 06.12.2016 passed by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal (Auxiliary) at Rajkot in MACP No. 1768 of 1999.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Tribunal (Auxiliary) at Rajkot
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has though partly allowed the claim petition of the original claimants holding them entitled to an amount of compensation of Rs 5,76,400/-,
however, has exonerated the respondent-Insurance Company.

Though the claim petition was partly allowed, holding the original claimants entitled to an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs 5,76,400/- with 6% interest and proportionate cost to be realized from the respondent no.1 only.
3. Learned advocate appearing for the appellant-original claimant has invited my attention to the order dated 20.07.2022 passed by the Coordinate Bench while admitting the appeal.

The only grievance which is voiced in the present appeal is the deletion of the respondent no. 3-Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2292/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined Company from the array of parties in the original proceedings.

As according to learned Advocate for the original claimant, the coverage of insurance as provided in the insurance policy was reflected as starting from 00.00 hours dated 20.01.1999 to midnight of 19.01.2000 whereas, the accident had occurred at 5:30 hours in the morning on 20.01.1989.
Thus, according to him, the Tribunal committed gross error in deleting the respondent no. 3-Insurance Company from the array of parties.
The appeal was admitted and the notice was issued upon the respondent no. 3- Insurance Company as well.
Noticing the order of admission passed by this Court, the record and proceedings have been called for.
4. Considering the issue involved, this Court had called upon the learned advocate for respondent no. 3-Insurance Company, Ms. Bhatt, appearing for respondent no. 3- Insurance Company.
She disputed the aforesaid facts by referring to the insurance policy produced on record.
She has submitted that before the Tribunal the respondent-Insurance company had moved an application at Exh-34, seeking deletion from the array of parties.
It was contended before the Tribunal that the accident had taken place on 20.01.1989 at around 5:30 hours.
The reference was made to the cover note dated 20.01.1999 wherein the time of issuance of cover note was mentioned as 4:00 pm.

It is in light of the aforesaid NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2292/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined facts, the Tribunal has proceeded to delete the respondent- Insurance company from the array of parties.
The Tribunal has also taken into consideration the insurance policy, and had arrived at a conclusion that the insurance policy was not in existence at the time of occurrence of accident.

The reliance was also placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Three Judges Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of New India Insurance Company Limited vs Bhagwati Devi and others,
reported in (1998) 6 SCC 534.

reported in (1998) 6 SCC 534

sentences.text: Learned Advocate had further pointed out that the aforesaid order dated 12.01.2009 passed by the Tribunal below Exh-34 has not been challenged.
In fact, the application was moved subsequently by the original claimants seeking permission of the Tribunal to join the respondent no. 3-Insurance company as party to the original claim proceedings.

She has therefore submitted that in absence of any challenge being made by the original claimants against the aforesaid orders by substantive proceedings, the aforesaid issue cannot be reagitated in the present appeal, which arises against the final impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
5. Learned advocate for the appellant has vehemently objected to the aforesaid submissions of learned advocate for respondent no. 3-Insurance company.

The attention of this Court was invited to the aforesaid orders passed by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2292/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/07/2025 undefined Tribunal below Exh-34 and 41.
The attention of this Court was also invited to the list of documents produced by the opponent-Insurance Company at the stage of the submission of written statement.

While referring to the cover note produced on record at mark 24/1,
learned advocate had pointed out that the said cover note was issued on 20.01.1999 and it was endorsed as the date of issuance of the cover note and the time of the issuance as 20.01.1999 at 4:00 pm.
In the aforesaid cover note, the acknowledgment was made with regard to the acceptance of the premium being realized against such coverage.

The attention of this court was invited to the insurance policy which is produced on record at mark 24/2 to point out that the formal policy was issued on 20.01.1999 wherein, the date of commencement of the insurance policy is indicated as 00.00 hours dated 20.01.1999 to midnight of 19.01.2000.

As regards the intimation letter addressed by the respondent-Insurance Company to the owner of the vehicle, it was pointed out that the aforesaid intimation letter was issued after the occurrence of accident on 06.09.1999 wherein, it has been clarified that the date and time of commencement of the risk and expiry to be considered in the policy should be 20.01.1999 at 4:00 p.m. till midnight of 19.01.2000 as mentioned in the original cover note dated 20.01.1999.
6.

He therefore, submitted that the Tribunal committed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2292/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined gross error in not considering the fact that the formal policy issued by the Insurance Company would govern the privity of contract and the respective liabilities.
He has further submitted that admittedly, the intimation letter has been addressed by the Insurance Company after eight months of occurrence of accident.
He has further pointed out that the aforesaid aspect has not at all been considered by the Tribunal while considering the issue of liability at the stage of pronouncement of final judgment and award.

He has relied upon the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure to contend that even in absence of any challenge being made to the non appealable orders passed pending suit, the aforesaid issues can always be looked into at the stage of appeal while examining the legality and validity of the final judgment and award.
He has therefore urged this Court to remand the matter back to the Tribunal for afresh consideration more particularly to examine the issue of liability.

7. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and having examined the findings and reasons assigned by the learned Judge, more particularly the order dated 21.11.2008 passed below Exh-34 and 41, in light of the order dated 20.07.2022 passed by Coordinate Bench of this Court issuing Notice to respondent No.3 Insurance Company is of the view that the aforesaid issue requires re- examination at the end of the Tribunal.

More particularly, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2292/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined after the cover note was issued, the Binduben Pradipbhai Desai (Legal Heirs ... vs Haji Mohammadsharif Hajikarimbaksh on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196230825/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: formal policy was issued by the Insurance Company on 20.01.1999, wherein the starting point of the insurance coverage was indicated as 00.00 hours dated 20.01.1999 to midnight of 19.01.1999.
As rightly pointed out by learned advocate for the appellant, the intimation letter was addressed by the Insurance Company, almost after period of eight months from the occurrence of accident.

Thus,
prima facie it appears that, at the time of occurrence of the incident i.e. at 5:30 a.m. on 20.01.1999,
as indicated in the formal policy, the insurance coverage was in existence.
However, considering rival submissions, this Court is of the view that the issue is required to be reexamined.

8. In the opinion of this Court, as regards the reliance placed by the Tribunal in the facts of the case,
while referring to the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bhagwati Devi (supra), the Tribunal committed error by not appreciating the legal principle that the view taken was that when there is a special contract mentioned in the policy details at the time when it was bought, it would be operative from that time and not fictionally from the previous midnight.

9. Recently the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Reliance Life Insurance Company Ltd. Versus Jaya Wadhwani, neutral citation 2024 INSC 10, has held that the date of proposal cannot be considered as date of Policy unless and until both NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2292/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined the initial date and issuance of Policy occurs on same date.

entities.text: Reliance Life Insurance Company Ltd. Versus Jaya Wadhwani, neutral citation 2024 INSC 10
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the Court clarified that for all intents and purposes, the date of issuance of the Policy shall be relevant date, and not the date of proposal or receipt issuance.

In the opinion of this Court,
considering the aforesaid legal principles and on appreciating the formal policy produced on record at Exh-28, it clearly indicates that the time of insurance coverage was to start from 00.00 hours on 20.01.1999, it was operative from that particular time.
The subsequent intimation letter addressed by the Insurance Company after the occurrence of accident, question arises whether the Insurance Company can shirk away from its liability.
On overall consideration, the issue needs to be reexamined on appreciation of evidence and not in the manner as approached by the Tribunal.
Hence, in exercise of inherent jurisdiction of this Court, it would be appropriate to remand, to meet ends of justice.

10. Since, the Tribunal had deleted the Insurance Company from the array of parties, the documents relied upon by the Insurance Company has not undergone the litmus test of provisions of Evidence law.
It has not been proved and established before the Tribunal.
Considering the aforesaid facts, the matter is directed to be re-examined afresh.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is hereby quashed and set aside and the matter is remanded back to the Tribunal to examine afresh.

The Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2292/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/07/2025 undefined Company is directed to be impleaded as party opponent in the original claim petition.
The Tribunal may extend sufficient opportunities to the respective parties to lead and prove their evidence.
11. With these observations, the First Appeal is allowed.
Let the record and proceedings be sent back forthwith to the concerned Tribunal.
12. Noticing the fact that the original claim petition relates to year, 2000, the Tribunal is requested to make endeavors to decide and conclude the hearing, preferably on or before 08.01.2026.
